The purpose of these two models was to compare the city parameter to identify potential differences in ND crash ratios between the two cities that could indicate effects due to dimmed lighting levels. • C2 roadways for nighttime crashes after 10:00 p.m. for after LED conversion (6). This model was intended to analyze the effect of dimmed light at Cambridge after 10:00 p.m. The model was developed using negative binomial regression with random effect based on nighttime crash data on C2 roadways for Cambridge and HPMS roadways for Somerville. Similarly, the researchers developed a daytime model for the same period and two models (daytime and nighttime) for the before-LED conversion period in an attempt to understand the dimming effects in a comprehensive manner. • C1 roadways for nighttime crashes after midnight and after LED conversion (7a), daytime crashes and after LED conversion (7b), nighttime crashes after midnight before LED conversion (7c), and daytime crashes before LED conversion (7d). The purpose of this analysis was to analyze the potential safety effect of dimmed light on C1 roadways in Cambridge after midnight. The models were developed using negative binomial regression with random effects. The comparison followed a similar approach as used for the general nighttime crash analysis using dimming 56 effect for the after conversion period and a pseudo dimming effect for the before LED period. This scenario focused on comparing the crash frequencies in Cambridge and Somerville based on the dimming schedule of the adaptive system at Cambridge. The purpose of this scenario was to understand better, by time period, how the dimmed lighting levels could have affected nighttime crash frequencies compared to a non-dimming LED system. Similar to the previous scenario, the researchers modeled C1 and C2 roadways in Cambridge (comparing with HPMS roadways in Somerville) using negative binomial regression with random effects. For the local roads in both cities, however, due to the limited information about traffic, the research team used LMMs to model ND crash ratios. 4.2.1.2.1 Nighttime Crashes at Local Roads after 8:00 P.M. The linear mixed modeling of ND crash ratio for the after LED conversion period showed that the city indicator was not a significant variable for the ND crash ratios (Table 14), indicating that the different LED lighting systems did not correlate to a significantly different ND crash ratio at a 0.05 level of significance (with a p-value of 0.12). The before LED conversion model (Table 15), however, showed that Cambridge had a slightly lower ND crash ratio on C3 roadways prior to the LED conversion compared to the local roads in Somerville. This result seemed to suggest that the dimmed light level on C3 roadways after the LED conversion potentially coincided with increased the ND crash ratios. However, although not significant, the parameter estimate in the after LED conversion model is well within the confidence limit of the estimate in the before LED conversion model, suggesting that the effect, if there was any, was not statistically significant.
